description: A four-channel stereo mixer with a gain and a voltage-controlled pan on each channel and one master level, which chains into another Hive placed beside it

params.text: Sets that channel's gain, marked in dB
Places that channel between the two outputs, hard left at fully counter-clockwise and hard right at fully clockwise; the centre is about 1.5dB down on either extreme
Sets the level of both outputs; the knob is squared before it is applied

inputs.text: That channel's left input; patch only this one and the same signal feeds both sides of the channel
That channel's right input; leave it unpatched and it takes whatever is at that channel's left input
Moves that channel's pan, 5V peak to peak for the full sweep, added to the pan knob and held inside it

outputs.text: The left side of the mix: the four channels at their gains and pan positions, scaled by MASTER and soft-clipped at ±10V
The right side of the mix: the four channels at their gains and pan positions, scaled by MASTER and soft-clipped at ±10V

notes: the MASTER knob comes up at zero, so nothing reaches the outputs until you raise it.
place a second Hive immediately to the right and this one's mix is added into that one's, but only while both of this one's output jacks are unpatched. Patch either output and the chain is cut.
the inputs are AC coupled by default, so a DC offset patched in will not reach the outputs. The menu turns that off.
menu: AC coupling — puts a 30Hz high-pass on every input, which takes DC offsets out of the mix; on by default, and found on the Hardware compatibility submenu
Clip Output ±10V — soft-clips both outputs at ±10V; on by default, and found on the Hardware compatibility submenu
